sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cétshamain is the Celtic festival better known as Beltane. People celebrate it on May 1. It was one of the four main festivals of the ancient Celtic year. Some argue the Celtic calendar was not found on the Continent. They say it represents only the Irish seasonal cycle. Beltane is an agricultural festival. It has roots in the cycle of grazing and planting. Beltane marked the beginning of summer. Cattle moved from the sheltered winter pastures to the mountain booleys. There the summer grass was fresh and green. Weather divination mattered at this festival. People read frost as a bad sign for the season.
